description:
CI RED on Linux; passes on macOS.

    thread 'main' panicked at cranelift-jit/src/backend.rs:243:
    can't resolve symbol fz_bitstring_is_binary

    matrix::to_string::run                  FAILED
    matrix::to_string_bitstring_panics::run FAILED

fz_bitstring_is_binary is declared in RUNTIME_SYMBOLS (src/extern_contract.rs:43)
but is absent from the ~80 hand-written builder.symbol(..) lines in
src/ir_codegen/backend.rs. On macOS the JIT falls back to dlsym over the process
image and finds the no_mangle export anyway; a Linux executable does not export
its symbols to dlsym, so there the same program dies.

WHY IT KEPT PASSING LOCALLY: this is a platform-dependent accident, not a
tolerance. Every symbol missing from that list is a landmine that only goes off
on Linux, and the six-target local gate cannot see any of them.

THE SHAPE (fz-5xp.21): RUNTIME_SYMBOLS was made the single provenance authority
for extern symbols in fz-5xp.3, and this list is a second copy of the same fact
that has already drifted. The fix is not to add one line -- it is to drive the
JIT registration FROM the authority, so a symbol declared there is registered by
construction and a symbol that is not declared cannot be registered.

Needs a test that fails for the right reason: a symbol in RUNTIME_SYMBOLS with
no JIT registration must be a compile-time or startup error, not a runtime
panic on one platform.
title: The JIT's symbol table is a second, hand-maintained copy of RUNTIME_SYMBOLS, and it is already missing one
